text:
Situation: Vancomycin hydrochloride injection from Hospira, Inc., a Pfizer Company, is recorded on FDA's shortage list as To Be Discontinued with an initial posting date of 2025-11-14. Corvale East holds 689 units at 29.1 units per day, providing 24 days on hand. Corvale General holds 786 units at 32 units per day, providing 25 days on hand. Detailed stock shows Corvale East: 1.25G vials 277 on hand (18.2 days) and 1G/200ML bags 412 on hand (29.7 days); Corvale General: Vancomycin 447.28 on hand (27.7 days) and Vancomycin Hydrochloride 338.74 on hand (21.3 days).

Why (FDA record): FDA's shortage list records Hospira, Inc., a Pfizer Company, vancomycin hydrochloride injection as To Be Discontinued with an initial posting date of 2025-11-14.

Our position: Current inventory provides approximately three to four weeks of supply across both campuses. No alternative manufacturer is currently on FDA's shortage list, but none of the identified suppliers disclose a manufacturing plant on their label.

Recommended actions:
1. Buyer to evaluate and qualify Avenacy, LLC, Baxter Healthcare Corporation, BluePoint Laboratories, Camber Pharmaceuticals, Inc., and Civica, Inc. for emergency purchase; requires P&T committee approval.
2. Buyer to request plant-of-origin documentation from each potential supplier; requires P&T committee approval.
3. Buyer to place initial orders with qualified suppliers to bridge the gap before Hospira supply is exhausted; requires P&T committee approval.

Not recommended: Switching to alternative agents or changing dosing protocols without P&T clinical review.
